key_insight: AI-based MRI radiomics showed good accuracy for preoperative detection of tumor deposits in rectal cancer, with pooled sensitivity of 76.5%, specificity of 79.0%, and AUC of 0.845.
clinical_relevance: Non-invasive tumor deposit detection could support preoperative risk stratification in rectal cancer; this study evaluates diagnostic imaging, not drug discovery.
method: Systematic review and bivariate diagnostic accuracy meta-analysis of nine studies involving 2,589 patients.
Evaluated MRI radiomics against histopathology as the reference standard.
Compared MRI sequences and radiomics-only models with models incorporating clinical or radiological features.
evidence_signal: Validation datasets yielded an AUC of 0.806; combined-feature models had higher sensitivity than radiomics-only models (84.2% vs 65.7%, p<0.001).
watch_item: MRI-sequence subgroup differences were not statistically significant, so superiority of T2WI plus DWI remains uncertain.
paper_title: AI-Based MRI Radiomics for Preoperative Detection of Tumor Deposits in Rectal Cancer: A Bivariate Diagnostic Accuracy Meta-analysis
